steps.title: Round 8 against round 9, hem at the shins
steps.note: Looks much better. i'd like the arm sleeve hems to have the same kind of flow that the hem at the shins have
steps.do: Look at round 9 of the clothing (J5): the hem shaking where it brushes the shins. The shake did not come from the shins touching the cloth. It came from the band that eases the robe from the waist toward the body: when a leg carried the hem far out through a slit, the band let go near the leg and grabbed the hem again as the leg passed, a hard yank on and off every step. The band is now a gentle pull that stays on, and the leg shapes taper toward the ankle so the hem no longer catches on air beside the shin. The hem's shake fell by about 40% at a normal walk (29 to 17 mm in the game test) and by about two thirds at a fast stride. Open the page in this step's files below and start with the slow-motion clip: round 8 on the left, round 9 on the right, the same two seconds of walking at a third of the speed. The page also has the full-speed clip and a still of round 8 over round 9 for the same moments of a step. One trade to look for: at a fast stride the back hem now flies a little higher behind the trailing leg; say if it should be heavier. Under this step, note 'yes' or what still looks wrong.
